author: Pecos Hank
description:
On April 23, 2026, a major tornado outbreak swept across parts of Oklahoma, Kansas, Missouri, and Iowa. Over the course of the day, I documented five tornadoes in Oklahoma — including the violent EF4 that struck Enid.

The video begins near Braman, Oklahoma, where a supercell produced four tornadoes, including two rare satellite tornadoes. Fortunately, the largest tornado weakened just south of Braman, sparing the town from a direct hit.
As that storm became embedded within a messy storm complex, another supercell rapidly intensified in the volatile atmosphere to the southwest near Enid, Oklahoma. This storm quickly produced a powerful tornado that would go on to cause substantial destruction across south Enid. The tornado remained on the ground for more than 30 minutes, carving a path through multiple communities south of the city. Extensive ground scouring
title: EF4 Tornado Strikes Enid Oklahoma - April 23, 2026
